facts.statement: Australosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylian.
facts.quote: taxon: Australosuchus

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Australosuchus is Australosuchus clarkae.
facts.quote: type_species: Australosuchus clarkae

facts.statement: Australosuchus was first described by Willis and Molnar in 1991.
facts.quote: authority: Willis & Molnar, 1991

facts.statement: Australosuchus lived during the Late Oligocene and Early Miocene epochs.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Oligocene–Early Miocene,

facts.statement: Australosuchus clarkae inhabited the Lake Eyre Basin in South Australia.
facts.quote: The type and only known species Australosuchus clarkae lived during the Late Oligocene and the Early Miocene in the Lake Eyre Basin of South Australia.

facts.statement: Australosuchus had the southernmost distribution of any mekosuchine, found only below 27°S latitude.
facts.quote: Australosuchus is among the mekosuchines with the southernmost distribution, being found exclusively at a latitude below 27°S

facts.statement: The name Australosuchus means "southern crocodile".
facts.quote: which is the basis for its scientific name meaning "southern crocodile".

facts.statement: Fossils of Australosuchus were discovered at Lake Palankarinna.
facts.quote: It was described in 1991 by Paul Willis and Ralph Molnar from fossil material discovered at Lake Palankarinna.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Australosuchus was cold-resistant, allowing it to live in freshwater systems too cold for other crocodilians.
facts.quote: One explanation suggests that Australosuchus was especially cold-resistant compared to contemporary forms like Baru and was thus able to inhabit freshwater systems too cold for its relatives.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen QM F16788 is a partial skeleton collected in 1975.
facts.quote: The holotype of Australosuchus is specimen QM F16788, a partial skeleton collected in 1975 that includes a nearly complete skull and lower jaw, various vertebrae, parts of the forelimbs and the dorsal armor.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the Etadunna Formation near Lake Palankarinna.
facts.quote: The holotype was unearthed from the Etadunna Formation near Lake Palankarinna, South Australia.

facts.statement: The genus name combines Latin and Greek roots meaning "southern crocodile".
facts.quote: The name of Australosuchus derives from the Latin "australis" and the Greek "suchus", which in combination mean "southern crocodile".

facts.statement: The species name clarkae honors Elaine Clark.
facts.quote: The species name on the other hand honors Elaine Clark, a dedicated supporter of the Riversleigh Research Project.

facts.statement: Australosuchus had a moderately broad and flattened skull.
facts.quote: Australosuchus was a medium-sized crocodilian with a moderately broad and flattened skull.

facts.statement: Willis estimated the length of Australosuchus to be around 3 meters.
facts.quote: Australosuchus was a medium-sized crocodilian, with Willis suggesting an estimated length of around 3 m.

facts.statement: The upper jaw contained 14 teeth on each side.
facts.quote: The maxillae are moderately broad and flat, containing 14 teeth on each side, the first six of which are placed along an alveolar process.

facts.statement: The lower jaw contained between 16 and 17 teeth.
facts.quote: The lower jaw contains between 16 and 17 teeth depending on the specimen

facts.statement: The vestigial fifth toe was robust and thicker than in other crocodilians.
facts.quote: The vestigial fifth toe is robuster and thicker than in other crocodilians.

facts.statement: Fossils of Australosuchus were mentioned in literature as early as 1968, before the genus was formally described.
facts.quote: Like many other mekosuchines, remains of this genus had been known long before its formal description, with the fossils of Australosuchus having been mentioned in literature as far back as 1968.

facts.statement: It is debated whether some fossils belong to the Mampuwordu Sands (Late Pliocene to Early Pleistocene) or were reworked from older strata.
facts.quote: Some fossils were initially described as stemming from the Mampuwordu Sands, which has been interpreted to be Late Pliocene to Early Pleistocene in age, but this is generally deemed unlikely.

facts.statement: The genus name Australosuchus means "southern crocodile".
facts.quote: El nombre del género Australosuchus significa "cocodrilo del sur".

facts.statement: It was described in 1991 from fossil materials discovered at Lake Palankarinna in South Australia.
facts.quote: Fue descrito en 1991 a partir de materiales fósiles descubiertos en el Lago Palankarinna en Australia del Sur.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Willis and Molnar in 1991.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Willis & Molnar, 1991

facts.statement: It belongs to the subfamily Mekosuchinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Mekosuchinae

facts.statement: Its fossil range spans from the Late Oligocene to the Early Miocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Oligoceno superior - Mioceno inferior

facts.statement: It lived between 27.3 and 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Burdigalian (27.3 to 15.98 million years ago)

facts.statement: All known records of Australosuchus come from latitudes below 27°S, whereas no other species like Baru are found south of 25°S.
facts.quote: all records of Australosuchus stem from below 27°S while no Baru are found south of 25°S.

facts.statement: Its southern range far exceeds the latitude of any modern crocodilian, such as the American alligator which ranges up to 36°N.
facts.quote: Yates highlights this range as significant in two ways. For one, it far exceeds the latitude at which any modern crocodilian is found at, with today's northernmost species being the American alligator which ranges up to 36°N.

facts.statement: A 2021 morphological analysis by Rio and Mannion placed Australosuchus outside Mekosuchinae as the sister taxon to Crocodylidae.
facts.quote: In the purely morphology based analysis by Rio and Mannion (2021), Australosuchus was found outside of Mekosuchinae as the sister taxon to the Crocodylidae.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses suggest Kalthifrons or a clade of Kalthifrons and Kambara might be more basal than Australosuchus.
facts.quote: In one other analysis, this position is occupied by Kalthifrons while in yet another a clade formed by Kalthifrons and Kambara appears as more basal.

facts.statement: Due to the lack of specialized adaptations like ziphodont teeth or a longirostrine skull, it is thought to have been a generalized member of Mekosuchinae.
facts.quote: Given the lack of any specialised adaptations such as ziphodont teeth or a longirostrine skull form, Australosuchus is thought to have been a more generalized member of the Mekosuchinae.
